messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixture of Normals
parts:
Also, don’t use that uniform prior on sigma, that’s no good for both statistical and computational reasons.  Use a soft constraint, for example lognormal.
A
On Nov 6, 2015, at 1:10 AM, sepehr akhavan <akhavan...@gmail.com> wrote:

I'm using RStan to fit a mixture of two normals.

data {
 int<lower = 1> K;
 int<lower = 1> N;
 real y[N];
}
parameters {
 simplex[K] theta;
 real mu[K];
 real<lower = 0> sigma;
}
model{
 real ps[K]; // place-holder for log component densities
 sigma ~ uniform(0.5, 1.5);
 mu ~ normal(0, 10);
 for (n in 1:N){
  for (k in 1:K) {
   ps[k] <- log(theta[k]) + normal_log(y[n], mu[k], sigma);
  }
  increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps)); // log_sum_exp(lp1,lp2) =    log(exp(lp1) + exp(lp2))
  }
}

I'd like to add a condition that mu[1] is less than mu[2]. How can I do that? In that a good idea to define mu as an ordered vector? In general, how can I add constraints between different cells of a vector? 

I'm very new to this group and I appreciate it if you could also give me feedback on whether these types of questions are appropriate to be asked in the group.

Thanks very much for your help,


--
